Here's the full picture:

---

All three are defined in `src/context.ts` and share the same `setDefaultContentType` helper (line 281), which builds `{ 'Content-Type': contentType, ...headers }` — meaning **the caller-supplied `headers` always win** (spread after the default, overriding it).

### `c.text()` — lines 682–694

Content-Type: `text/plain; charset=UTF-8` (the `TEXT_PLAIN` constant, line 279).

**Has a fast path**: if there are no pre-set headers, no status override, no extra args, and the response isn't finalized, it short-circuits to a bare `new Response(text)` — no `Content-Type` header at all (line 688). The browser/client gets the native default. This is the only one of the three with this optimization.

### `c.json()` — lines 708–721

Content-Type: `application/json` (no charset suffix).

Always calls `JSON.stringify(object)` on the value before passing it to `#newResponse`. No fast path — always goes through the full response builder.

### `c.html()` — lines 723–733

Content-Type: `text/html; charset=UTF-8` (charset included, unlike `application/json`).

Uniquely accepts `string | Promise<string>`. When given a Promise (e.g., from JSX async components), it calls `resolveCallback(html, HtmlEscapedCallbackPhase.Stringify, ...)` to resolve HTML-escaped content before constructing the response. The other two are synchronous only.

### Summary table

| Method | Content-Type | Charset | Body transform | Fast path |
|--------|-------------|---------|----------------|-----------|
| `c.text()` | `text/plain` | `UTF-8` | none | yes — bare `new Response(text)` when no other state |
| `c.json()` | `application/json` | none | `JSON.stringify()` | no |
| `c.html()` | `text/html` | `UTF-8` | none (but awaits Promises) | no |

In all three, the caller can override the content-type by passing a `headers` object — it's spread *after* the default in `setDefaultContentType` so caller-supplied values take precedence.
